text:
maya: FYI we reproduced an SSE duplicate on reconnects from a single-tenant customer. steps and quick logs below.

alex: wat happened?

maya: flow: client connects -> events 1,2 -> connection stalls (no FIN) at edge for ~40s -> client reconnects with Last-Event-ID=1 -> server resumes from 1 -> client receives 1 twice (duplicate).

sam: do we know whether server re-sent 1 or proxy replayed buffered bytes?

maya: evidence points to proxy. tcpdump on edge shows original stream bytes still in socket send buffer at reconnect. proxy then flushed those bytes into the new connection.

olivia: so upstream socket half-open and proxy didn't detect client close, right?

maya: exactly. our resume code assumes upstream connection was closed/clean. this proxy buffering produces an extra copy when it forwards leftover data.

infra-bot: Deploy job #deploy-1723 completed on edge-proxy pool-3 at 2026-03-20T09:10:12Z :white_check_mark:

alex: which proxy image + kernel patch? any recent changes to keepalive settings?

maya: proxy v2.7.1, keepalive 60s, SO_LINGER off. Kernel bumped from 5.15.8 -> 5.15.11 in last rollout; write coalescing changes noted in release notes.

sam: candidate mitigations: lower keepalive on edge, enable TCP_USER_TIMEOUT, or toggle TCP_NODELAY for SSE sockets (disable Nagle).

olivia: will NODELAY blow up packet counts for many small events?

alex: it will increase packets but reduce small-write latency. for low-volume SSE streams tradeoff might be acceptable.

maya: bigger issue: telemetry gap. console shows reconnect+resume but not "proxy-queued-bytes" so support can't tell if duplicates were proxy-caused.

sam: can we detect duplicates server-side (if id seen within N seconds) and log an event?

alex: risky: some clients expect inclusive Last-Event-ID semantics and want the overlap. server dedupe could hide legitimate replays. prefer getting proxy metrics.

olivia: short-term plan suggestions?

maya: propose: 
- Canary reduce proxy keepalive to 15s for the affected pool.
- Add proxy metric: per-connection queued_bytes and export to prometheus.
- Add console dashboard tile & alert for queued_bytes > 32KB for >30s.
- As last resort, optional server-side dedupe that can be toggled per tenant.

alex: agree on proxy-first approach. infra toggle + metric export seems low risk.

sam: @infra-team can we flip keepalive on pool-3 for a 2h canary?

infra-bot: @infra-team config change request: set keepalive=15s on pool-3. Approvers: ops-leads.

maya: repro script I used (local stub):
```
# server: emit small events 1..5 with sleeps
while true; do for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do echo "data: $i\n\n"; sleep 1; done; done
# proxy: forward but pause draining for 40s to simulate stuck socket
```
Observed: when client reconnects quickly, proxy flushes buffered chunk 1 to new socket resulting in duplicate.

alex: good repro. console UX ask: can we show a "possible duplicate" flag on reconnects if proxy queued_bytes > threshold?

olivia: yes, but need proxy to emit queued_bytes first. I can add a dashboard tile and support tooltip explaining expected behavior.

sam: I'll open small PR to proxy repo to expose queued_bytes and add a config knob for NODELAY and TCP_USER_TIMEOUT. link: https://git.rex/proxy/changes/485

alex: infra canary schedule?

infra-bot: scheduled canary: pool-3 keepalive change at 2026-03-20T16:00:00Z. Rollback window 2h.

maya: I'll run the customer repro against the canary endpoints and report back here.

olivia: I'll own the console tile + alert (low-pri dashboard workstream).

sam: I'll own the proxy PR and the prometheus metric export.

alex: I'll coordinate approvals and postmortem checklist if this recurs.

maya: also adding a short note to our resume docs that Last-Event-ID inclusive semantics can lead to duplicates if proxies buffer. saves support time.

olivia: good call. Maya, please ping once you validate canary. I'll prepare a small support blurb for the tenant about brief canary windows.

maya: will do. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
